title: Greek Yogurt & White Bean Power Bowls
displayTitle: Greek Yogurt & White Bean Power Bowls
seoTitle: Greek Yogurt & White Bean Power Bowls | Firefighter Meal
shortDescription: Warm white beans and quinoa with a lemon Greek yogurt sauce, feta, and vegetables
subtitle: Warm white beans and quinoa with a lemon Greek yogurt sauce, feta, and vegetables
description: Warm white beans and quinoa are topped with cucumber, tomato, and feta, then finished with a generous lemon Greek yogurt sauce instead of a thin vinaigrette. It is a balanced, fully vegetarian bowl built to hold its own at dinner.

steps.title: Cook the quinoa
steps.instruction: Rinse quinoa and cook according to package directions. Fluff with a fork and hold covered.

steps.title: Warm the beans
steps.instruction: Heat olive oil in a skillet over medium. Add garlic and cook 30 seconds, then stir in white beans and warm through, 5–6 minutes, seasoning with salt and pepper.

steps.title: Build the yogurt sauce
steps.instruction: Whisk Greek yogurt, lemon juice, olive oil, and dill if using in a bowl with a pinch of salt until smooth.

steps.title: Hold everything at the right temperature
steps.instruction: Keep quinoa and beans covered and warm. Keep the yogurt sauce, feta, cucumber, tomatoes, and red onion cold and separate until serving.

steps.title: Build the bowls
steps.instruction: Layer quinoa and white beans in each bowl, then top with cucumber, cherry tomatoes, red onion, and feta.

steps.title: Finish with the sauce
steps.instruction: Spoon a generous amount of lemon Greek yogurt sauce over each bowl just before serving.

steps.title: Hold for call interruptions
steps.instruction: If tones drop mid-cook: turn off direct heat and cover white beans and quinoa — hold at 140°F in a warm cabinet or 200°F oven, never below 140°F for more than 30 minutes cumulative. Log hold time on the pan with a grease pencil. If tones drop after service, cover hot food and keep sides on low heat or ice as appropriate. On return, spot-check proteins at safe internal temp before reopening the line.

steps.title: Pack down leftovers safely
steps.instruction: Cool greek yogurt white bean power bowls and hot components in a shallow baking dish within two hours — food left out too long isn't safe to eat. Label with date; reheat proteins to 165°F minimum before second shift. Store cold components separately so textures survive overnight.

proTips: Prep tip: Salt the yogurt sauce a little more than tastes right when raw — cold quinoa and beans mute seasoning.
Rookie tip: Keep the sauce separate until serving so the bowl doesn't turn soupy sitting on the line.
Add kalamata olives for crews who want a saltier, more traditional Greek profile.
tonightSpread: Main: Greek yogurt and white bean power bowls
Sides: Warm pita, simple side salad
Condiments: Extra lemon wedges, kalamata olives
Set hot components closest to the crew; cold crunch and toppings at the far end of the line.
Keep a backup tray at 200°F for firefighters returning from a run.
leftovers: Cool greek yogurt white bean power bowls in shallow pans within two hours; label with date and reheat to 165°F before second shift.
Store cold sides separately — hot and cold stacked overnight ruins texture.
Keep the yogurt sauce separate from the grains so leftovers don't turn watery.
whyCrewsLikeIt: It eats like a Mediterranean plate the crew already likes, but the yogurt-and-bean combination pushes the protein well past a typical vegetable bowl.
mealPrepNotes: Make-ahead: cook quinoa and beans up to two days ahead. Storage: keep grains, beans, cold vegetables, and yogurt sauce in separate containers up to 4 days. Reheating: warm quinoa and beans together; add cold vegetables and sauce at serving time.
substitutions: Use chickpeas instead of white beans.
Use farro or brown rice instead of quinoa.
Use dairy-free yogurt for a lighter-dairy version (protein count will drop).
